verdictBasis: 1 blocker, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 4 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. REJECT.
verdictStatement: Four of the five repairs are real and two of them are the best work in this series. The identity union is closed and tagged, its classMap covers all eight taxonomy classes exactly in both directions, SONAME-ABI is confined to libc as its own text demands, and comparison is bound to the resolved object rather than to prose — no version-or-digest string survives anywhere. The B4 repair kills the harness-capability escape twice over, routes inability-to-observe to qualification failure or platform removal rather than a skipped cell, and adds a retained event schema that makes traces checkable instead of narrative. The selector grammar is well built: four required members, or-joins forbidden, and the exact 'apfs-or-hfs-plus' collapse I flagged against v2 now named as a mustNot, with stems barred from freezing an allowlist — which structurally discharges my own v2 finding. The carrier resolves to one table and one binding point, verified reciprocally against DR-101's live v8. The verbatim carries and the eight-class taxonomy are byte-exact against live, and the document has tripled in size since v1 without acquiring a single number. What fails is where the grammar sends the half it reserves. v2 drew this boundary correctly and indefinitely — 'a later G22 packet that populates members is a different artifact' — a class, with no name and no designee. v3 deleted that sentence and replaced it with platform-tcb-population-packet, named as the ownerArtifact of all eight reserved selectors and described as an already 'named independently reviewed artifact'.
